author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: A reader can ask the veterinarian directory for one specialty and get back only the veterinarians holding it, on the page and in the machine-readable list alike. Without a specialty, both surfaces behave exactly as today.
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> renders the directory listing only veterinarians holding that specialty, paged as the unfiltered directory is today
the specialty name is matched in full and case-insensitively; a partial name such as part of a specialty's name matches no veterinarian
every pagination link on the filtered /vets.html page carries the specialty parameter, so following any page link keeps the same filter in force
/vets?specialty=<name> returns the machine-readable veterinarian list carrying only the veterinarians holding that specialty, matched the same way
a specialty that no veterinarian holds yields the ordinary page or machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200 on both surfaces, never an error
an empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces, mirroring the empty owner search
without the specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as they do today, including paging and the machine-readable document shape
a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed when the directory is filtered by any one of them
non_goals: any on-page control for choosing a specialty: no form, dropdown, link, or menu on either surface
free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits
filtering by more than one specialty in a single request
paging the machine-readable list, which stays unpaged
reinstating REQ-VET-002, which stays withdrawn and whose id is not reused
notes: One slice ships the filtering acceptance of both REQ-VET-003 (page) and REQ-VET-004 (machine-readable list). REQ-VET-004 also makes the /vets route a supported surface: its unfiltered behavior already holds and needs a regression test only, not new production code. NG-9 narrowed - see docs/adr/2026-08-11-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed.md. Three product questions were left open in the PRD rather than consulted, per the dispatch: an on-page control, multiple specialties per request, and telling an unrecorded specialty name apart from one nobody holds. Follow-up outside this agent's write scope: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new ADR, and system-design.md Contracts should cite REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 on VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, and Vets.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The Specialty filter is an attribute filter inside the existing vet feature package: no new package, type, or layer, and no cross-package edge. Its filtering shape mirrors owner search - a Spring Data derived finder takes the value plus a Pageable, and the controller normalizes the request value at the HTTP boundary. Two things are genuinely new ground and are now recorded in durable memory. First, the vet repository is the only cached one in the codebase, and the filter's key would come from an unauthenticated query parameter (system-design.md Contracts, plus the uncached-reads ADR). Second, no template here preserves a filter across pagination links - the owner list drops its search value - so REQ-VET-003's link requirement has no precedent to copy. Case folding moves into the query rather than the column (system-design.md Persistence, plus the case-folding ADR), which keeps the match identical on all three vendors and avoids repeating the recorded PostgreSQL owner-search divergence.
integration_points: /vets.html gains an optional specialty request parameter; the view model gains a specialty attribute so the template can rebuild it into every pagination link
/vets gains the same parameter, stays unpaged, and fills the existing Vets wrapper from the filtered collection
VetRepository gains a filtered overload pair mirroring the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) pair: one Collection-returning finder for /vets, one Page-returning finder for /vets.html
vetList.html pagination links move from concatenated query strings to Thymeleaf's URL-parameter syntax, which encodes the value and omits it when null
no template, message bundle, or navigation entry gains a control for choosing a specialty - the URL is the only way in

patterns.description: derived finder taking the match value plus a Pageable and returning a Page - the shape the specialty finder follows, with the IgnoreCase keyword added and equality rather than StartingWith
blank search value normalized at the HTTP boundary: strip the value, treat empty as the broadest read. The specialty parameter mirrors this exactly, per the acceptance criteria
the findAll()/findAll(Pageable) overload pair the two filtered finders mirror; note @Cacheable belongs to these two only
counter-example, do not copy: owner pagination links carry only the page number and silently drop the search value. REQ-VET-003 requires every vet pagination link to carry the specialty
the match folds case in the query via the derived-query IgnoreCase keyword, never by relying on a column collation
the two filtered finders carry no @Cacheable annotation

risks.risk: The join over vet_specialties can list a veterinarian more than once on a filtered page, and a duplicate would also distort the page count
risks.mitigation: Cover the multi-specialty vet with the acceptance test that asserts a single appearance; add Distinct to the derived finder if the query yields duplicates

risks.risk: A request-derived value reflected into pagination hrefs by string concatenation would be emitted unencoded, which is the current link style in this template
risks.mitigation: Build the links with Thymeleaf's @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=...)} parameter syntax: it URL-encodes the value and omits a null parameter, so the unfiltered page keeps today's link shape

risks.risk: Copying the owner-search empty-result branch would reject an unmatched specialty with a form error instead of an empty list
risks.mitigation: Both surfaces answer HTTP 200 with an empty veterinarian list; the vet controller gains no rejectValue branch and no error view

risks.risk: Annotating the filtered finders @Cacheable for symmetry would let any caller mint one cache entry per distinct string, against a cache with no size limit and no eviction
risks.mitigation: Leave them unannotated per the uncached-reads ADR; the cache-sizing question stays Open Question 5 and is not settled here

risks.risk: The page and the machine-readable directory drifting in how a blank or absent value is handled
risks.mitigation: Normalize once in a private VetController helper that both handlers call, and route both to the same repository finders

notes: Trust boundary: specialty is external input arriving at the HTTP boundary. Normalization is trim, then treat blank as absent. No allowlist of specialty names is applied, because the PRD deliberately leaves an unrecorded name and one nobody holds indistinguishable, both answered with an empty list. No length cap is needed either: the value is not a cache key, reaches the database only through a parameterized derived query, and is escaped on output by Thymeleaf and by the URL-parameter syntax. Architecture-principles check: the controller's trim-and-blank handling is request adaptation, not a business rule, and the selection rule itself lives in the repository query - no new business rule enters a controller. Rejected alternative: one JPQL finder guarded by ':specialty is null or upper(name) = upper(:specialty)'. It is heavier than the derived-query pattern the codebase already uses, and the blank-to-absent normalization would still belong at the boundary. Durable memory written this dispatch: system-design.md Contracts now cites REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 on Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController, records the cache scope, and records the query-side case folding under Persistence; the stale Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less is closed by REQ-VET-004; the ADR index gained rows for the NG-9 narrowing ADR and the two new ADRs. Autofix audit: the log carries no design-doc-autofix records, so nothing to audit. Coverage claims here rest on direct reads and grep of the vet and owner packages; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, which is the weaker basis.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty value reaches the database only through Spring Data derived finders (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, both overloads in VetRepository). No JPQL or SQL text is composed, so the value is always a bound parameter. Matches the control in security-principles.md and the SQL-injection row of the threat model.

Reflected XSS in vetList.html: all five pagination links were rewritten from the string-preprocessing form @{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'} to the parameterized link form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link-expression query parameter values and th:href escapes the attribute output, so a payload such as specialty="><script>alert(1)</script> is emitted percent-encoded inside a quoted attribute and cannot break out. The change strictly improves on the preprocessing form it replaced. Swept the whole templates/ tree: no th:utext and no remaining __${...}__ preprocessing anywhere, so no second instance of this class exists.

Reflected value on the error path: a specialty that surfaced in an exception message would render through error.html's th:text="${message}", which escapes. No unescaped sink for the value exists on any surface.

No allowlist and no length cap is defensible here. The value is never a cache key (see below), never composes a filesystem or classpath path, never reaches a log line or a URL the server fetches, and reaches the database as a bound parameter compared against a three-row lookup table. The residual concern is resource consumption, which is outside the reviewable class set and is not a weakening of the recorded baseline.

Cache-key growth: the ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-11-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-uncached.md holds under inspection. @Cacheable("vets") appears only on the two unfiltered reads; both new caller-parameterized finders are unannotated, so an unauthenticated caller cannot mint entries in the unbounded vets cache. The decision is the correct one given CacheConfiguration declares no size limit or eviction.

Boundary normalization is at the HTTP edge and shared: requestedSpecialty() strips and maps empty to null once, and both surfaces call it, so the HTML page and the JSON route cannot diverge in what they match or in when the filter is considered absent.

Exposed surface: no new route. Both handlers are the existing /vets.html and /vets mappings gaining an optional read-only query parameter. The JSON response body is the same Vets projection as before, filtered — no field or entity becomes newly reachable, so there is no new data exposure.

No secrets in the diff: swept the change set for credential-shaped material (token, password, secret, key, and the datasource property names). The only key-like hits are Java identifiers and ADR prose. No property file, no build file, and no configuration was touched.

Supply chain: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and gradle/ are unchanged in the change set, so no dependency was added, upgraded, or repointed and no new CVE surface is introduced by this slice. No dependencyCheck task is configured in this project; the check reduces to the unchanged dependency declarations.

author: product-requirements-expert
answer:
Criterion 7 covers the rendered pagination URL. The empty specialty= parameter on the unfiltered page is a defect against REQ-VET-003; change the template so a blank or absent specialty is omitted from every page link. Do not re-point the new test at the current behavior — keep it red until the template is fixed.

Three grounds, each independently sufficient.

1. Criterion 3 bounds the authorization. It reads 'every pagination link on the FILTERED /vets.html page carries the specialty parameter'. The owner's decision behind it — 'pagination links carry the parameter so filtered pages stay navigable' — states the purpose and the limit in the same sentence. The mandate to touch the links extends to the filtered page and no further. An empty parameter on an unfiltered page serves no navigability need, so nothing authorizes it.

2. Criterion 7 is a regression clamp, not a content clamp. 'Behave exactly as they do today, including paging' is the broadest wording available and takes the whole observable boundary of the two endpoints. The href the directory hands the reader is the paging behavior — following it is the paging action. Reading 'behave' as 'the response body's list of veterinarians' would let the slice change status codes, headers, and links freely, which is plainly not what the owner asked for when they said 'exactly as they do today'. Narrowing here would widen the slice's licence, not narrow it.

3. The design agrees. The design-block at line 8 asserts twice, as fact, that the parameter syntax 'omits it when null' (integration_points entry 4, risks entry 2). The intended behavior at every level of the record — requirement, owner decision, design — is omission on the unfiltered page. The implementer verified the mechanism does not deliver it. That is a mechanism failing a stated intent, which is the definition of a defect, not a rediscovered requirement.

On the argument that the URL is mechanism and therefore outside the PRD: the PRD does not specify the query-string shape, and it should not. It specifies that the unfiltered directory behaves as before. The URL shape is the mechanism by which that requirement is met or broken, exactly as a status code is. system-design.md#contracts carries both endpoints as boundary surface.

On the content argument the request raises: correct that content is unaffected, and that a bookmarked /vets.html?page=1&specialty= would render the same list, since criterion 6 makes an empty value equivalent to an absent one. That is why this is a low-severity defect and not a broken page. It is still a defect: the unfiltered directory emits into address bars, bookmarks, and history a URL naming a filter the reader never asked for.

Cost, since it falls on the implementer: the fix is in vetList.html, already in file_targets, and invalidates the three approvals. That is the correct price. A production change always re-enters review — do not weigh the re-review against the requirement.

PRD clarification applied so the test has a spec anchor: docs/prd.md gains one Done-when bullet under REQ-VET-003 — 'given no specialty at all, when the directory offers a link to another page, then that link asks for no specialty, as before.' It makes criterion 7's existing meaning explicit and adds no scope; no Non-Goals row is touched and no superseding prd-entry is needed.

Resume: fix the template, keep theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldCarryNoSpecialtyWhenTheDirectoryIsUnfiltered asserting hrefs with no specialty= parameter, re-run the full gate, append build-pass and the review-plan.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The unfiltered/filtered branch is now a full ternary duplicated five times, once per pagination link (`${filtered} ? @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=...)}`). Each line restates both URL shapes, so the five links must be read and compared expression-by-expression to confirm they agree; a future change to the URL shape (a new query param, a path change) has to be applied identically in ten places instead of one, and a single missed branch would silently regress the same bug this fix pass corrected. The pre-existing template already repeated the plain `@{...}` expression five times, so the duplication itself is not new, but this change doubles the expression each line carries.
findings.fix: Hoist each link's href into a named `th:with` variable on the outer `<div>` (e.g. `hrefFirst`, `hrefPrev`, `hrefNext`, `hrefLast`, and a per-iteration expression for the numbered links), computed once each with the `${filtered} ? ... : ...` ternary, so the five branching decisions sit together near `filtered` and each `<a th:href="...">` reduces to referencing the precomputed value. This keeps the fix template-only (no controller change) while separating the branching logic from the repeated markup.

approved_aspects: th:with="filtered=${specialty != null}" correctly hoists the branch condition once instead of repeating the null-check inline five times
The fix is confined to the template, matching the PRD-ruled defect's scope and file_targets
Comment above the div explains why the branch exists, giving cold-read context for the non-obvious null-parameter behavior
Both branches are pinned by tests (theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldCarryTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldCarryNoSpecialtyWhenTheDirectoryIsUnfiltered)
checkFormat and checkstyleMain/checkstyleTest pass clean on the fix delta

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Implementer's claim verified against src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html: all five pagination links choose between two whole link expressions with a ternary on the boolean `filtered`; the attacker-controlled value never leaves the (specialty=${specialty}) parameter slot of an @{...} expression. No raw concatenation, no string-built href, so Thymeleaf still owns both URL-encoding of the query parameter value and HTML-attribute escaping of the rendered attribute. The reflected-value surface the prior pass flagged for examination is clean; no reflected XSS.

The `filtered` guard reads the same normalized value the query and the links use: VetController.requestedSpecialty (VetController.java:90-96) folds absent, empty, and whitespace-only to null before the model attribute is set, so the parameter-presence branch cannot diverge from the filter-applied branch. An unfiltered page emits no specialty= at all; a blank-only request is indistinguishable from an absent one on both surfaces.

Class sweep over the reflected-output class across src/main/resources/templates/: no th:utext and no [(...)] unescaped inlining anywhere in the template tree, and `specialty` is reflected nowhere in vetList.html outside the five link expressions. The one instance examined was the only instance.

Injection surface unchanged and safe: VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is a Spring Data derived query (VetRepository.java:71,83), so the specialty is bound as a JPA parameter, never concatenated into JPQL or SQL. The absence of an allowlist and of a length cap on the unauthenticated parameter remains acceptable at this trust boundary — the value reaches only a parameterized query and a URL-encoded link parameter, and unbounded length is a resource-consumption concern outside this review's severity bar, consistent with the prior pass's assessment.

Filtered finders remain uncached, matching docs/adr/2026-08-11-specialty-filtered-vet-reads-uncached.md: neither findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase overload carries @Cacheable, and the Javadoc records the security ground (a request-derived cache key in a size-unlimited cache). The unbounded-cache-entry-minting path stays closed.

No secrets in the fix delta: the four changed files carry no credential-shaped literal under any naming (token, password, secret, key or otherwise); the only added constants are the test's page size and vet count.
No dependency, build, or configuration change in the delta, so the supply-chain surface cleared by the prior pass is unmoved.
